title: Physics — Types of electromagnetic waves

meta_desc: GCSE Combined Science (AQA) practice covering Physics — Types of electromagnetic waves, specification section 4.6.2.1.
final_note: You worked through Physics — Types of electromagnetic waves — 5 specification statements.

concepts.def: A transverse wave that transfers energy from the source of the wave to an absorber. Electromagnetic waves can travel through a vacuum, so no substance is needed to carry them.
A wave in which the oscillations are at right angles to the direction in which the wave transfers energy. All electromagnetic waves are transverse.
A wave moves energy from one place to another without moving matter from one place to another. The particles or fields oscillate; they are not carried along.
The source is the object that emits the wave; the absorber is the object that takes in its energy. A lamp is a source of light; a black surface it shines on is an absorber.

The electromagnetic spectrum has no gaps: wavelength changes smoothly from very long to very short, and the seven named groups are labelled regions of one continuous range, not seven separate wave types.
The distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave. Radio waves have the longest wavelength in the spectrum and gamma rays the shortest.
The number of waves passing a point each second. Across the spectrum frequency rises as wavelength falls, so gamma rays have the highest frequency and radio waves the lowest.
The only group of electromagnetic waves the human eye can detect. Within it, red has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest, so the group runs red to violet.
A space containing no matter. All types of electromagnetic wave travel at the same velocity through a vacuum (space) or air, which is why sunlight reaches the Earth across empty space.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes an electromagnetic wave?
options: A transverse wave that transfers energy from source to absorber
A longitudinal wave that transfers energy to an absorber
A transverse wave that transfers matter to an absorber
A transverse wave that needs air to carry its energy
mcqs.explain: The specification defines electromagnetic waves as transverse waves that transfer energy from the source of the waves to an absorber.

mcqs.q: A transmitter sends radio waves to a distant aerial. What is transferred, and in which direction?
options: Particles of matter, from the transmitter to the aerial
Energy, from the source of the wave to the absorber
Energy, carried along by the air between them
Sound, from the transmitter to the radio aerial
mcqs.explain: The wave transfers energy from the source (the transmitter) to the absorber (the aerial).

mcqs.q: How do the speeds of radio waves, visible light and gamma rays compare in a vacuum?
options: Gamma rays are fastest because they carry the most energy
Radio waves are slowest because their wavelength is longest
All of them travel at the same velocity in a vacuum
Visible light is faster than the radio waves are
mcqs.explain: All types of electromagnetic wave travel at the same velocity through a vacuum (space) or air.

mcqs.q: The electromagnetic spectrum is described as continuous. What does this mean?
options: It is made of seven separate waves with gaps between them
It jumps in seven fixed steps like rungs on a ladder
Every group in it can be detected by the human eye
There are no gaps between one group and the next
mcqs.explain: Wavelength changes smoothly across the spectrum, so the groups merge into one another with no gaps.

mcqs.q: Which list gives the electromagnetic groups in order from longest wavelength to shortest?
options: Radio, microwave, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, X-rays, gamma
Radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays
Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Radio, microwave, infrared, violet, red, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma
mcqs.explain: This is the order given in the specification, going from long to short wavelength.

mcqs.q: Moving across the spectrum from radio waves towards gamma rays, what happens to wavelength and frequency?
options: Wavelength decreases and frequency increases
Wavelength and frequency both increase together
Wavelength rises while the frequency falls
Both wavelength and frequency decrease
mcqs.explain: Going from long to short wavelength is the same as going from low to high frequency.

mcqs.q: A hot radiator emits infrared radiation. Why can a person in the room not see it?
options: The radiator is not hot enough to glow visibly yet
The eye can see infrared, but only in a dark room
Infrared travels too fast for the eye to detect
Our eyes only detect visible light, not infrared
mcqs.explain: Eyes only detect visible light and so detect a limited range of electromagnetic waves.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best example of energy being transferred by an electromagnetic wave?
options: A loudspeaker making the nearby air vibrate
Warm air rising above a heater in a room
Sunlight warming a dark road surface
A spoon warming inside a mug of hot tea
mcqs.explain: The Sun is the source and the road is the absorber; energy crosses empty space as an electromagnetic wave.
